usage: certipy [-v] [-h]
               {account,auth,ca,cert,find,parse,forge,relay,req,shadow,template}
               ...

Active Directory Certificate Services enumeration and abuse

positional arguments:
  {account,auth,ca,cert,find,parse,forge,relay,req,shadow,template}
                        Action
    account             Manage user and machine accounts
    auth                Authenticate using certificates
    ca                  Manage CA and certificates
    cert                Manage certificates and private keys
    find                Enumerate AD CS
    parse               Offline enumerate AD CS based on registry data
    forge               Create Golden Certificates or self-signed certificates
    relay               NTLM Relay to AD CS HTTP Endpoints
    req                 Request certificates
    shadow              Abuse Shadow Credentials for account takeover
    template            Manage certificate templates

options:
  -v, --version         Show Certipy's version number and exit
  -h, --help            Show this help message and exit
Certipy v5.1.0 - by Oliver Lyak (ly4k)

--help.help: Show this help message and exit

--version.help: Show Certipy's version number and exit

-account.help: Account to target. If omitted, the user specified in the target will be used

-add-manager.help: Add a new manager (CA Manager) to the CA

-add-officer.help: Add a new officer (Certificate Manager) to the CA

-aes.help: AES key to use for Kerberos Authentication (128 or 256 bits)

-application-policies.help: Specify application policies for the certificate request using OIDs (e.g., '1.3.6.1.4.1.311.10.3.4' or 'Client Authentication')

-archive-key.help: Specify CAX Certificate for Key Archival. You can request the cax cert with 'certipy req -cax-cert'

-backup.help: Backup CA certificate and private key

-bloodhound.help: Output result as BloodHound data for the custom-built BloodHound version from @ly4k with PKI support

-ca.help: Name of the Certificate Authority to manage

-ca-password.help: Password for the CA PFX file

-ca-pfx.help: Path to CA certificate and private key (PFX/P12 format). If not specified, a self-signed root CA will be generated

-cax-cert.help: Retrieve CAX Cert for relay with enabled Key Archival

-cert.help: Load certificate from PEM or DER file

-config.help: CA configuration string in format Machine\CAName

-configuration.help: Configuration to apply to the certificate template. If omitted, a default vulnerable configuration (ESC1) will be applied. Useful for restoring an old configuration

-crl.help: LDAP path to a CRL distribution point

-dc-host.help: Hostname of the domain controller. Required for Kerberos authentication during certain operations. If omitted, the domain part (FQDN) specified in the account parameter will be used

-dc-ip.help: IP Address of the domain controller. If omitted, it will use the domain part (FQDN) specified in the target parameter

-dc-only.help: Collects data only from the domain controller. Will not try to retrieve CA security/configuration or check for Web Enrollment

-dcom.help: Use DCOM Enrollment instead of RPC

-device-id.help: Device ID of the Key Credential Link to target

-disable-template.help: Disable a certificate template on the CA

-dn.help: Distinguished name of the user provided in the command line. Useful for cross domain authentication

-dns.help: Set the DNS hostname for the account (e.g., computer.domain.local)

-dns-tcp.help: Use TCP instead of UDP for DNS queries

-domain.help: Domain name to authenticate to (extracted from certificate if omitted)

-dynamic-endpoint.help: Prefer dynamic TCP endpoint over named pipe

-enable-template.help: Enable a certificate template on the CA

-enum-templates.help: Relay to /certsrv/certrqxt.asp and parse available certificate templates

-export-password.help: Password to protect the output PFX/P12 file

-force.help: Don't prompt for confirmation before applying changes. Use this option to apply modifications without user interaction.

-forever.help: Don't stop the relay server after the first successful relay

-format.help: Input format: BOF output or Windows .reg file (default: bof)

-group.help: Group to which the account will be added. If omitted, CN=Computers,<default path> will be used

-hide-admins.help: Don't show administrator permissions for -text, -stdout, -json, and -csv

-http-port.help: Web Enrollment port (default: 80 for http, 443 for https)

-http-scheme.help: HTTP scheme to use for Web Enrollment (default: http)

-interface.help: IP Address of interface to listen on (default: 0.0.0.0)

-issue-request.help: Issue a pending or failed certificate request

-issuer.help: Issuer to include in certificate. If not specified, the issuer from the CA cert will be used

-k.help: Use Kerberos authentication. Grabs credentials from ccache file (KRB5CCNAME) based on target parameters. If valid credentials cannot be found, it will use the ones specified in the command line

-key.help: Load private key from PEM or DER file

-kirbi.help: Save Kerberos TGT in Kirbi format (default is ccache)

-ldap-channel-binding.help: Use LDAP channel binding for LDAP communication (LDAPS only)

-ldap-port.help: Port for LDAP communication (default: 636 for ldaps, 389 for ldap)

-ldap-scheme.help: LDAP connection scheme to use (default: ldaps)

-ldap-shell.help: Authenticate with the certificate via Schannel against LDAP

-ldap-simple-auth.help: Use SIMPLE LDAP authentication instead of NTLM

-ldap-user-dn.help: Distinguished Name of target account for LDAP authentication

-list-templates.help: List all enabled certificate templates on the CA

-no-channel-binding.help: Disable channel binding for HTTP connections

-no-hash.help: Don't request NT hash from Kerberos

-no-ldap-channel-binding.help: Don't use LDAP channel binding for LDAP communication (LDAPS only)

-no-ldap-signing.help: Don't use LDAP signing for LDAP communication (LDAP only)

-no-save.help: Don't save Kerberos TGT to file

-no-skip.help: Don't skip previously attacked users (use with -forever)

-nocert.help: Don't include certificate in output (key only)

-nokey.help: Don't include private key in output (certificate only)

-oids.help: Show OIDs (Issuance Policies) and their properties

-old-bloodhound.help: Output result as BloodHound data for the original BloodHound version from @BloodHoundAD without PKI support

-on-behalf-of.help: Use a Certificate Request Agent certificate to request on behalf of another user

-out.help: Output filename for the exported certificate/key

-output.help: Filename prefix for writing results to

-pass.help: Set the password for the account

-pfx.help: Path to certificate and private key (PFX/P12 format)

-pfx-password.help: Password to protect the output PFX file

-print.help: Print Kerberos TGT in Kirbi format to console

-ptt.help: Submit TGT for current logon session (Windows only)

-published.help: Consider the comma separated list of template names as published in AD

-remove-manager.help: Remove an existing manager (CA Manager) from the CA

-remove-officer.help: Remove an existing officer (Certificate Manager) from the CA

-retrieve.help: Retrieve an issued certificate specified by a request ID instead of requesting a new certificate

-sam.help: Set the SAM Account Name for the account (e.g., computer$ or username)

-save-configuration.help: Save the current template configuration to a JSON file. This creates a backup before making changes or documents the current settings. If not specified when using -write-configuration or -write-default-configuration, a backup will still be created.

-serial.help: Custom serial number for the certificate

-sid.help: SID of the user provided in the command line. Useful for cross domain authentication

-sids.help: Consider the comma separated list of SIDs as owned for vulnerability assessment

-smime.help: Specify SMIME Extension that gets added to CSR (e.g., des, rc4, 3des, aes128, aes192, aes256)

-spns.help: Set the Service Principal Names for the account (comma-separated)

-stdout.help: Output result as text directly to console

-subject.help: Subject to include in certificate, e.g. CN=Administrator,CN=Users,DC=CORP,DC=LOCAL

-target.help: protocol://<IP address or hostname> of certificate authority. Example: http://ca.corp.local for ESC8 or rpc://ca.corp.local for ESC11

-target-ip.help: IP address of the target machine. If omitted, it will use whatever was specified as target. Useful when target is the NetBIOS name and cannot be resolved

-template.help: Path to template certificate to clone properties from

-text.help: Output result as formatted text file

-upn.help: Set the User Principal Name for the account (e.g., user@domain.local)

-use-owned-sids.help: Use the SIDs of all owned principals as the user SIDs

-user.help: Logon name for the account to target

-username.help: Username to authenticate as (extracted from certificate if omitted)

-vulnerable.help: Show only vulnerable certificate templates based on nested group memberships

-web.help: Use Web Enrollment instead of RPC

-write-configuration.help: Apply configuration from a JSON file to the certificate template. Use this option to restore a previous configuration or apply custom settings. The file should contain the template configuration in valid JSON format.

-write-default-configuration.help: Apply the default Certipy ESC1 configuration to the certificate template. This configures the template to be vulnerable to ESC1 attack. It accepts an optional argument for the target sid that should get ESC1 permissions (default S-1-5-11 for authenticated users). CAREFUL: If you specify a SID of an account not under your control, you lose the ability to restore!

account_action.help: Action to perform: create (new account), read (view account properties), update (modify existing account), delete (remove account)

file.help: File to parse (BOF output or .reg file from registry export)

shadow_action.help: Operation to perform on Key Credential Links: list (view all), add (create new), remove (delete specific), clear (remove all), info (display detailed information), auto (automatically exploit)
